newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port transshipment cargo up 31 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port transshipment cargo up 31 pct.

text.p: Transshipment traffic at Colombo Port rose 31 percent in the first nine months of this year to 699,128 twenty-foot equivalent containers, the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) said on Monday.
The number of container ships calling at Colombo, south Asia's transshipment hub, rose 18 percent to 1,795 over the same period, an SLPA spokesman said.
Transshipment traffic accounted for 72 percent of the number of containers handled by the port in this period, he said.
Total cargo handled by the port rose 17 percent to 15.2 million tonnes up to September this year compared with the year before, the spokesman said.
The present capacity of the port, which last year handled just over a million containers, is 1.6 million containers.

Colombo handles some 23 percent of cargo from the Indian subcontinent but faces stiff competition from ports like Singapore for increased cargo volumes anticipated with the liberalisation of India's economy, shipping officials said.
